title: The Future of GTA Online After GTA 6 Launches
summary: GTA Online, based on GTA 5, will continue to be supported after GTA 6 launches. A new version of GTA Online may come in 2027, per the CEO of Twitch. GTA...
body_markdown:
GTA Online has been immensely successful since launching with GTA 5, offering new heists, surprisingly involved roleplay servers, and just a place to hang out with friends – you know, by crashing cars, mowing down pedestrians, blowing stuff up and whatnot. Normal friend stuff.


If you’re an avid GTA Online player, you may be wondering: “Hold on, after GTA 6 launches, what the heck am I gonna do? Are they going to make me abandon everything I built up in Los Santos and start over in Leonida?”


Good news: the current version of GTA Online *will* be supported beyond GTA 6.


This comes from Take-Two Interactive’s annual shareholder meeting, where they answered several burning questions about GTA 6’s November 19th release on consoles.


At the meeting, Take-Two stressed that GTA 6 will launch as single-player only, meaning there will be no new online at all to speak of.


At least for now.


That’s because we also recently learned via comments Twitch CEO Dan Clancy gave to Bloomberg that the multiplayer version of GTA 6 would, indeed, come sometime in 2027.


While not official, those comments hint at the fact there may soon exist two GTA Online experiences —one based on GTA 5 and one based on GTA 6— that could be supported simultaneously and indefinitely. That would be great news for those who have invested a lot into GTA Online over the last 10 years as well as for those who are hungry to jump into a whole new multiplayer experience.


Only time will tell for the future of GTA multiplayer, so make sure you’re tuned to this blog for more GTA 6 updates, especially as we get closer to launch.


In the meantime, if you’re looking to cultivate a proper GTA atmosphere, you can’t go wrong with the[Pacific Skyline controller.](https://www.turtlebeach.com/products/pacific-skyline-controller) With sky blue buttons against pink pastel palms and a hidden skyline design that reveals itself with RGB, you’ll be fully immersed in the dreamy, serene vibes of the coast. Until you pick up your controller and start committing armed robbery, that is.
